name: Forearm Plank
instructions: Lie face down and place your forearms on the floor with elbows directly under your shoulders, hands pointing forward.
Tuck your toes under and lift your hips off the floor so your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
Brace your abs, squeeze your glutes, and keep your neck neutral by gazing at the floor just ahead of your hands.
Hold the position for the prescribed time while breathing steadily, then lower your knees to finish.
formCues: Keep hips level with shoulders, neither sagging nor piking up
Brace the core as if preparing to take a punch to the stomach
Squeeze glutes and quads to lock the whole body rigid
commonMistakes: Letting the lower back sag and the hips drop
Holding the breath instead of breathing steadily
Raising the hips too high into a pike position

name: Hanging Leg Raise
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, arms fully extended and body relaxed.
Brace your core and posteriorly tilt your pelvis to keep the body from swinging.
Keeping your legs straight, raise them in front of you until they reach hip height or higher.
Pause briefly at the top, then lower your legs under control back to the start without swinging.
formCues: Initiate by curling the pelvis up, not just lifting with the hip flexors
Keep the descent slow and controlled to eliminate swing
Keep a firm grip and engaged lats for shoulder stability
commonMistakes: Using momentum and swinging the body to throw the legs up
Only raising the legs partway with no pelvic tilt
Dropping the legs quickly instead of controlling the lowering phase

name: Lying Leg Raise
instructions: Lie flat on your back with legs extended and hands placed under your glutes or flat by your sides.
Press your lower back gently into the floor and brace your core.
Keeping your legs straight, raise them until they are roughly vertical at about 90 degrees.
Lower the legs slowly and stop just before they touch the floor to keep tension, then repeat.
formCues: Keep the lower back flat against the floor throughout
Move slowly, especially on the lowering phase
Avoid arching the back as the legs descend
commonMistakes: Letting the lower back arch off the floor at the bottom
Using momentum to bounce the legs up
Bending the knees excessively to make it easier

name: Bicycle Crunch
instructions: Lie on your back with hands lightly cupped behind your head and knees bent, feet off the floor.
Brace your core and lift your shoulder blades off the ground.
Rotate your torso to bring one shoulder toward the opposite knee while extending the other leg straight.
Switch sides in a smooth pedaling motion, bringing the opposite shoulder toward the opposite knee.
Continue alternating sides under control for the prescribed reps.
formCues: Rotate from the torso rather than yanking on the neck
Keep the lower back in contact with the floor
Move with control instead of racing through reps
commonMistakes: Pulling on the head and straining the neck
Going too fast and losing rotation through the torso
Lifting the lower back off the floor

name: Russian Twist
instructions: Sit on the floor with knees bent and hold a dumbbell or plate at chest level with both hands.
Lean your torso back to about 45 degrees and brace your core, keeping your spine long.
Lift your feet off the floor for more challenge, or keep your heels down for an easier version.
Rotate your torso to one side, bringing the weight beside your hip, then rotate to the other side.
Continue alternating sides under control for the prescribed reps.
formCues: Rotate through the trunk, not just the arms
Keep the chest up and spine long, avoiding rounding
Control the tempo to keep tension on the obliques
commonMistakes: Swinging the arms while the torso stays still
Rounding the lower back as you lean away
Moving too fast and losing core tension

name: Cable Woodchop
instructions: Set a cable pulley to a high position and grip the handle with both hands.
Stand side-on to the machine with feet shoulder-width apart, arms extended up toward the pulley.
Brace your core and pull the handle down and across your body toward the opposite hip, rotating your torso.
Pivot the rear foot as you rotate, keeping your arms relatively straight throughout the chop.
Return slowly along the same path to the start, then complete all reps before switching sides.
formCues: Drive the rotation from your core, not just your arms
Allow the back hip and foot to pivot with the movement
Keep the arms long and control the return phase
commonMistakes: Pulling with the arms instead of rotating the trunk
Using too much weight and losing control
Keeping the feet planted and twisting only at the lower back

name: Mountain Climbers
instructions: Start in a high plank position with hands under your shoulders and your body in a straight line.
Brace your core and keep your hips level with your shoulders.
Drive one knee toward your chest, then quickly switch to drive the other knee forward.
Continue alternating legs in a running motion while keeping the upper body stable.
Maintain a steady rhythm for the prescribed time.
formCues: Keep the hips low and level, avoiding piking them up
Keep shoulders stacked directly over the wrists
Maintain a tight core throughout the movement
commonMistakes: Letting the hips bounce or pike up with each knee drive
Placing the hands too far forward and straining the shoulders
Bouncing on the feet instead of driving the knees with control

name: Floor Crunch
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hands lightly behind your head or crossed over your chest.
Brace your core and press your lower back gently into the floor.
Curl your shoulder blades off the floor by contracting your abs, exhaling as you lift.
Pause briefly at the top, then lower your shoulders back down under control.
formCues: Curl the ribcage toward the pelvis rather than pulling on the neck
Keep a small space between chin and chest
Exhale on the way up to maximize the contraction
commonMistakes: Pulling on the head and straining the neck
Using momentum to jerk up instead of a controlled curl
Lifting the entire back off the floor like a sit-up
